2. One Dhirendra Lal Sharma being the predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 1-4 as plaintiff instituted. Other Suit No. 222 of 1983 in the court of the then Munsiff (now Assistant Judge), Upazilla Ramu. District Cox's Bazar impleading the predecessor of the opposite party No.1 and 'opposite party No. 2 and 3 as defendants praying for declaration that the ekrarnama created in favour of the plaintiff is collusive, manufactured, forged, void and the order passed by the revenue officer of Upazilla Ramu in R.M. Case No. (102/1974-75)/(280/1980-83)and all proceeding thereon including the order dated 2.11.83 be declared illegal, ineffective, null and void. The plaintiff alleged that the suit land originally belonged to defendant No.1, who sold the same to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 8.2.1971 and that there was no talk of any reconveyance nor there is existence of any agreement or ekrarnama for reconveyance of the suit land. The defendant No.1 filed R.M. Case No. (102/1974-75 )/(280/1982-83)before the circle officer (Rev) 280/1982-83 alleging that the transaction was a mortgage and not out and out sale and on such statement the defendant No. 1 claimed redemption of the mortgaged property and that the circle officer (Revenue) allowed the case treating the transaction as mortgage and hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant No. I contested the suit by I filing a written statement contending that the defendant No. I filed a case for redemption of mortgage before the revenue authority, who by the order dated 2.1 1.83 passed an order for redemption of the suit land and accordingly the instant suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The plaintiff then preferred Other Appeal No. 81 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar. The teamed Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Cox's - Bazar. who heard the said appeal, concurred with the decision of the trial court that the deed of sale Ext. 4 and the deed of ekrarnama Ext. D were written by the same scribe and signed by the same attesting witnesses. The trial court, however, found that the ekrarnama was not a registered document and thereby the case is not covered by section 95A of the Sate Acquisition And Tenancy Act. The learned lower appellate court, however, found that the defendant may institute a suit for Specific Performance of Contract before a competent court and by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.9.89 allowed the appeal in part. The learned appellate court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court in part and declared that the order dated 2.11.80 passed in R.M. Case No.  (102/1974-75)/(280/1982-83)is unauthorized and ineffective and declared "এতদ্বারা তফশীলেল জমিতে ৮/২/৭১ ইং তারিখের একরার নামা (প্রঃডিঃ) মূলে ১নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক চুক্তি কবলে ফেরত কবলা পাওয়ার শর্ত সাপেক্ষে বাদীর খরিদা স্বত্ব উচ্চারন করা গেল। " 

 7. Mr. Samiran Dasgupta, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf the learned Advocate Mr. Rabi Shankar Chakraborty submits that ekrarnama Ext. 13 was never executed by the plaintiff and that the scribe of the ekrarnama as P.W. 2 deposed that the plaintiff did not put his signature in his presence and thus the execution of the ekrarnama was not proved. The learned Advocate for the petitioner  however submits, that the signatures of the plaintiff appearing on the ekrarnama was not the signature of the plaintiff and the plaint containing the signature of the plaintiff and the alleged ekrarnama Ext. D containing the signature of the plaintiff shows that they are not the product of the same hands. The learned Advocate, however, agreed that the lower appellate court was not correct in holding .that because the ekrarnama was not registered, the transaction was not covered under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate however submits that the courts below committed serious error of law in not granting a decree in favour of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff never executed the ekrarnama. The learned Advocate has also submitted that the attesting witness Profulla Kumar Sharma denied his signature on the ekrarnama Ext. D as P.W. 3 but the courts below committed an error of law in holding that Profulla Kumar Sharma was the attesting witness in Ext. D and thou the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable. 

 8. Mr. J.B.M. Hassan, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, on the other hand, supports the decision of the trial court and submits that deed of sale accompanied by an unregistered ekrarnama constitutes complete usufructuary mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the trial court is correct in its view that the transactions by the kabala ,Ext. 4 and the ekrarnama Ext. D shows that the transaction is a complete usufructuary mortgage and not an out and out sale. The learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Abdul Sheikh and other Vs. Puspa Rani and others reported in I BLC (AD) 228. 

 9. 1 have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the impugned judgments of both the courts below. Both the courts below on consideration of the evidence on record came to concurrent finding of fact that Ext. 4 and Ext. D were written by the same scribe and common witnesses became the attesting witnesses in both the documents. Both the courts have considered the plaintiffs signature appearing in the plaint and his signature appearing in ekrarnama and found that the signatures are the product of the same hand. I have also examined the signature appearing in the ekrarnama Ext. D it appears that they are product in same hand. I have also considered the signature of the scribe P.W. 2 and attesting witnesses P.W. 3 appearing in the sale deed Ext. 4 and in the ekrarnama Ext. D and that the finding of the courts below that P. W. 2 wrote both the documents Ext. 4 and Ext. D and P. W. 3 was the attesting witness in both Ext. 4 and Ext. D appears to be correct. This evidence shows that Ext. 4, the sale deed and Ext. D the ekrarnama were contemporaneous documents and the transaction together constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In the decision as referred to above, our Appellate Division held "The clear legislative intent of section 95A is that cases of sale attended with agreement for reconveyance whether or not registered would be within the ambit of complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of 7 years and provisions of section 95(4)(5) would apply to such transfers. A contrary view would clearly make the provision of section 95A nugatory and frustrate its purpose: Their lordships further noticed that section 95A conceives a case where there is a transaction of sale with or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess and enjoy the Usufruct of a parcel of land. Even though there is contrary intention expressed in the document of transfer, the transaction would be considered as a complete usufructuary mortgage for a maximum period of 7 years. Their Lordship noticed a decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Abdul Gani reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 wherein it was pointed out with reference to the background of the legislation that the underlying object of the-provision of section 95A is to rescue a raiyat from the clutches of the money lenders who taking advantage of the poverty of the raiyat force to enter into a disadvantageous deal by means of getting a registered kabala from the raiyat, themselves executing an unregistered agreement for reconveyance. In view of the aforesaid decision, the present case is clearly attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the lower appellate court committed an error of law in taking the view that the deed of reconveyance being unregistered, the case is not covered by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned District Judge was therefore not correct in its view that to attract the provision of 95A - of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, both the deeds being the sale cited and the deed of reconveyance must be registered to attract section 95A of S.A.T. Act, I am of the view that a transaction of an out and out sale attended by an unregistered deed of reconveyance constitutes a complete usufructuary mortgage for a maximum period of 7 years and the mortgagor is permitted to pray for recovery of possession by way of redemption of mortgage It is true that the impugned judgment was in favour of the defendant and thus did not file any revision before this court but the power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is wide enough to exercise its supervisory power to pass a necessary and proper order to meet ends of justice when the matter has been brought before this court by any of the parties to the suit. In the facts of' the case the trial court committed no error of law in dismissing the suit. The lower appellate court committed an error of law in allowing the  appeal in part in declaring that the order dated 2.11.80 passed in R.M. Case No.  (102/1974-75)/(280/1982-83)  is unauthorised and ineffective is hereby set aside and also the declaration that "এতদ্বারা তফশীলেল জমিতে ৮/২/৭১ ইং তারিখের একরার নামা (প্রঃডিÑ মূলে ১নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক চুক্তি প্রবলে ফেরত কবলা পাওয়ার শর্তসাপেক্ষে বাদীর খরিদা স্বত্ব উচ্চারন করা গেল।"
